question: What is the main purpose of giving a patient a purgative?

options.A: To increase the absorption of water in the large intestine
options.B: To slow down gastrointestinal motility and prevent diarrhea
options.C: To promote bowel movements and relieve constipation
options.D: To neutralize excess stomach acid and soothe ulcers

explanation: You've got this! Purgatives are simply given to help clear the bowels and get things moving when a patient is constipated. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h1)

question: How do gentle laxatives usually differ from strong purgatives?

options.A: Laxatives cause rapid and violent fluid evacuation of the bowel
options.B: Laxatives produce softer, more formed stools with less urgency
options.C: Laxatives can only be administered through intravenous lines
options.D: Laxatives completely paralyze the smooth muscle of the colon

explanation: Think of laxatives as gentle helpers for mild relief, whereas strong purgatives bring fast, watery results! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h1)

question: During normal digestion, what is the main job of the large intestine?

options.A: Breaking down complex proteins into simple amino acids
options.B: Producing bile acids needed for fat digestion
options.C: Absorbing water and electrolytes from waste material
options.D: Secreting large amounts of digestive enzymes into chyme

explanation: Great job! As food waste travels through the colon, the large intestine's primary task is to pull water and minerals back into the body. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h2)

question: Why does waste material become hard and dry when it moves too slowly through the colon?

options.A: The liver stops producing mucus to lubricate the intestinal walls
options.B: The anal sphincter closes too tightly and squeezes out moisture
options.C: Bacteria in the lower bowel multiply rapidly and dry out the waste
options.D: Extra time allows the colon to absorb more water than normal

explanation: Makes sense, right? If stool stays too long in the colon, the body keeps drawing out water, leaving the waste dry and tough to pass. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h2)

question: How do osmotic purgatives work inside the gut?

options.A: Coating the intestinal lining with a thick oily film
options.B: Directly irritating the nerve endings inside the colon wall
options.C: Drawing water into the bowel lumen through high osmotic pressure
options.D: Swelling up with water to stretch the muscle fibers of the colon

explanation: Spot on! Osmotic agents act like a magnet, drawing fluid into the intestine to soften the stool and make it move easily. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which type of drug works mainly by swelling up with water to stretch the intestinal wall and trigger movement?
explanation: You got it! Bulk-forming agents absorb fluid and expand, increasing stool size so the bowel naturally contracts to push it out. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h3)

question: What must patients always drink plenty of when taking bulk-forming purgatives?
explanation: Always remember this clinical pearl: bulk-forming drugs need lots of water to expand safely, otherwise they can cause a blockage! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h4)

question: A patient with severe kidney failure is prescribed a magnesium-based laxative. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Consult the doctor because magnesium can accumulate dangerously in renal failure
options.B: Switch the medication to a bulk-forming agent without telling the physician
options.C: Advise the patient to take the drug with twice as much table salt
options.D: Administer the medication immediately as ordered without any extra precautions

explanation: Brilliant! Kidneys filter out magnesium; if they aren't working well, the mineral builds up to dangerous levels. Always check with the prescriber. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do stimulant purgatives mainly get things moving in the gut?

options.A: By irritating the intestinal mucosa and stimulating muscle contractions
options.B: By absorbing excess gas bubbles trapped inside the stomach folds
options.C: By lowering blood pressure to reduce fluid filtration in the gut
options.D: By coating the lower bowel with a soothing layer of mineral oil

explanation: Stimulants gently nudge the local nerves and muscles in the colon wall, forcing them to contract and push waste along. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why are stool softeners frequently given to patients recovering from major surgery?

options.A: They completely stop all intestinal gas and bloating
options.B: They prevent painful straining during bowel movements
options.C: They speed up the healing of abdominal skin incisions
options.D: They kill harmful bacteria hiding in the large intestine

explanation: Exactly! Keeping the stool soft saves healing surgical patients from painful bearing down and straining. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h5)

question: When is a strong purgative commonly used in a clinical setting?

options.A: Replacing lost electrolytes after severe dehydration
options.B: Clearing the bowel before a colonoscopy or surgery
options.C: Lowering high fever during a malaria infection
options.D: Treating severe bacterial infections in the bloodstream

explanation: You're doing great! Strong purgatives are standard practice for cleaning out the intestinal tract before medical scopes or operations. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why must the bowel be completely cleared before a diagnostic colonoscopy?

options.A: To stimulate the pancreas to produce more digestive enzymes
options.B: To absorb any remaining local anesthetic used in the operating room
options.C: To prevent the patient from feeling hungry during the procedure
options.D: To give the physician a clear, unobstructed view of the intestinal lining

explanation: A clean colon lets the doctor clearly spot polyps, redness, or tiny lesions without stool blocking the way. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the major danger of giving a purgative to a patient with a bowel obstruction?

options.A: It will immediately cure the blockage
options.B: It can cause the bowel to rupture
options.C: It causes severe high blood pressure
options.D: It turns the stool completely black

explanation: Watch out for this! Forcing muscle contractions against a blocked pathway raises pressure dangerously and can tear the bowel wall. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h7)

question: In which of these situations is giving a strong purgative UNSAFE?

options.A: When a patient has acute abdominal pain of unknown origin
options.B: When a patient needs to avoid straining after childbirth
options.C: When managing mild constipation caused by dietary changes
options.D: When preparing an adult patient for a scheduled colonoscopy

explanation: Never guess with belly pain! Unexplained pain could mean appendicitis or a blockage—giving a purgative here can be disastrous. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h7)

question: A patient admits to taking over-the-counter stimulant laxatives every day for months. What should you advise?

options.A: Explain that daily use can cause the bowel to lose its natural function and suggest seeing a doctor
options.B: Assure the patient that daily laxative use is completely safe and healthy
options.C: Tell the patient to switch to drinking palm oil instead of taking pills
options.D: Encourage the patient to double the daily dose to get a faster result

explanation: Spot on. Relying on stimulants long-term makes the bowel lazy. Patients need professional guidance to safely restore normal habits. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h8)

question: What is the best everyday advice a nurse can give to help prevent chronic constipation?

options.A: Take a strong saline purgative every morning before breakfast
options.B: Reduce all fluid intake to allow stools to form more slowly
options.C: Avoid eating local foods like beans and green vegetables
options.D: Increase intake of water, dietary fiber, and physical activity

explanation: Simple and natural is best! Drinking water, eating fiber, and staying active keep the digestive tract happy and regular. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h8)
